cursor.note: THE DEFECT WAS A DICTIONARY DEFAULT. `data.get("members_so_far", [])` cannot tell an absent key from an empty list, so when the corpus retired that key on 2026-08-28 in favour of `members_derived_by` — a RULE saying how the membership set is derived — the gate read the retirement as 'the roster is empty' and reported one fault once per skill directory: 21 findings over the live corpus, 15 of them false. A reader that swallows the absent case does not go quiet; it goes LOUD in the wrong place, and the fifteen false reds are what a peer would have had to sort by hand every run. THE DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION, and it is the thing worth reading in a year: the pre-build reader, lifted out of git HEAD into a temp module and handed a fixture commons whose skill.json is valid JSON with no membership key, returns ([], None) — an empty set and NO FAULT. That pair is the whole bug in two values. The post-build reader over the same fixture returns a fault naming the file and what it lacks. WHAT THE VOYAGE RETIRED, AND WHY THAT IS NOT A WEAKENING. Once membership is DERIVED by listing skills/ and `chartered` is derived by filtering that same listing, `every_chartered_skill_is_on_the_roster` cannot be given a world that reds it — `chartered - membership` is empty BY CONSTRUCTION. That is a green earned by arithmetic rather than by the world, and Law 8 calls it worse here than a red, because a peer leans on it without re-checking. Its successor `every_skill_directory_carries_a_charter` makes the same comparison from the end that can still disagree, and a tooth proves it reds when a charter is removed. The property the retired lane asserted did not stop being true — it stopped being a CHECK and became physics, which is Law 4 doing its job one lane at a time. The retirement carries a note naming its successor, the date and the reason, in the code and in the charter; nothing was deleted silently. THE PREDICTION WAS MADE BEFORE THE BUILD AND HELD EXACTLY: 21 -> 6. The six survivors are /ruled chartered-but-not-installed plus the five bin/cmd entries no charter's invoke names, name for name the six recorded at cast on 2026-09-09. The hypothesis named the inverse defect as the worse one — a count BELOW six would mean the fix had swallowed a real finding — and the name-by-name compare is what rules it out rather than the count. THREE BUGS THIS VOYAGE UNCOVERED IN ITS OWN INSTRUMENTS AND FIXED IN PLACE (bounds ruling 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage). (1) test_the_gate_lists_what_it_proved asserted `len(record) >= 8`; retiring a lane would have been a NUMBER QUIETLY LOWERED, which is exactly the shape this ticket was cast against. It now names the lanes, so a retirement is an edit to a list a reader can see. (2) A tooth appended at the end of the proof file NEVER RAN — TEETH was a module-level comprehension over globals() evaluated above it — and the file printed a confident '19/19 teeth green' over a test that had never executed. Collection moved inside the runner at the true end of file. This is the declared-teeth-vs-printed-teeth trap, and it is corpus-wide: 189 of 211 proofs carry a hand-rolled __main__ of the same shape. (3) The WATCHME probe FIRED SPURIOUSLY on its first live read, reporting reds_from_one_fault=7, because it counted the gate's ABSOLUTE red total and six of those were the corpus's standing out-of-bounds findings. Rewritten to run the corpus twice — real node class vs starved — and report the DELTA: one fault, one red, on one named lane. A probe that had not been made to fire would have carried that error quietly for its whole horizon. ONE THING THE CHART DID NOT KNOW. The survey left open whether cairn/tools/edges reads membership. It was settled by MEASUREMENT rather than by reading: edges' proof was run after the reader change and BEFORE its fixture was touched, and it was green — gather does not consult membership, only the gate does. Its fixture was updated anyway, because cairnmap.gather runs over that world and the world has to be one that still exists.

window.note: PROVEME — the prediction made before the build held exactly: `cairnmap --gate` dropped from 21 findings to 6, and the 6 are name-for-name the ones the ticket put out of bounds (/ruled chartered-but-not-installed, five bin/cmd entries no charter's invoke names). 20/20 teeth green twice; edges 9/9 twice. skill_roster() is now skill_membership(), deriving from the node class's own `members_derived_by` rule and naming THREE faults, each exactly one red: no rule declared (the ABSENT-KEY shape `.get(key, [])` swallowed), `members_so_far` back, or a rule that stops naming skills/. `every_chartered_skill_is_on_the_roster` is RETIRED with a note naming its successor — under derivation it compares a set against a superset of itself, a green arithmetic guarantees, which Law 8 calls worse here than a red. Its falsifiable half survives as `every_skill_directory_carries_a_charter`. THREE BUGS THE VOYAGE UNCOVERED AND FIXED (bounds ruling 2026-09-09): (1) the proof's lane floor was `len(record) >= 8`, a count that cannot say WHICH lane went missing — now the lanes are named, so retiring one is an edit to that list; (2) TEETH was collected at import time, so a tooth appended at the end of the file never ran and the file printed a confident 19/19 over it — now collected at call time; (3) the WATCHME probe's first reading counted the gate's ABSOLUTE red total and fired at 7, six of which were the corpus's standing out-of-bounds findings — rewritten to read the DELTA a substituted starved node class adds, which is the only attributable number.

window.note: The probe is armed at cairn/tools/cairnmap/probes/the_roster_fault_is_one_finding.py, beside what it watches. It reads the gate's own record twice over the live corpus — once with the real node class and once with a starved one that says nothing about members — and reports the DELTA: how many reds ONE membership fault adds, and which lanes it adds them to. One fault must add exactly one red, on exactly the_skill_membership_rule_is_declared, and must close the derived lane rather than red it. THE FIRST LIVE READ CAUGHT ITS OWN BUILDER: written as an ABSOLUTE count it reported reds_from_one_fault=7 and fired, because six of the seven were the corpus's standing out-of-bounds findings and had nothing to do with membership. Rewritten as the delta it reads reds_live=6, reds_starved=7, reds_from_one_fault=1, added_lanes=['the_skill_membership_rule_is_declared'], fires=False. Verified capable of firing: test_the_watchme_probe_is_armed_and_can_be_made_to_fire hands the reading function a substitute reporting the pre-build behaviour and gets fires=True. `enough` needs 10 gate runs across at least 3 distinct corpus states, so it cannot clear on the day it was armed.

window.note: RETREAT, and the reason is a finding about /sail rather than about this build. Neither the BUILDME->PROVEME nor the PROVEME->WATCHME crossing carried `proven_by`, so no crossing on this ticket named the proof that proves it. The clearance gate refused the PROVED crossing with two lacks — [proof_named] and [hollow_evidence_absent] — and `cairn test --hollow 7aed0fd0ba29 --seal` refused for the same root cause: 'no crossing on ticket 7aed0fd0ba29 names a proof, so there is no instrument to run against the reverted build'. The proof existed and was green and sealed the whole time; what was missing was the crossing SAYING SO. /sail's step 4 says to seal under the tester and never says to name the proof on the crossing, so the builder learns this by being refused at the last gate — which is where the cost is highest. Retreating to PROVEME to re-cross carrying the name is the honest repair: the record shows the voyage went back and said what proves it, rather than a hand writing evidence into a gate's input. Defect filed against /sail: `/sail never tells the builder to pass proven_by`.
